questions.question_text: What is the perimeter of a rectangle with length $8\text{ cm}$ and width $5\text{ cm}$?

options.why: This adds one length and one width, omitting their opposite sides.
This multiplies length by width instead of adding the outside lengths.
This counts both lengths but only one width: $8+8+5=21$.

questions.question_text: What is the perimeter of a square with side length $6\text{ cm}$?

options.why: This counts only one of the four equal sides.
This counts only two of the four equal sides.
This squares the side length instead of adding four side lengths.

questions.solution_text: All four sides are $6\text{ cm}$. $P=4\times6=24\text{ cm}$.

questions.question_text: What is the perimeter of a triangle with side lengths $5\text{ cm}$, $7\text{ cm}$ and $9\text{ cm}$?

options.why: This adds $5+7$ and omits the $9\text{ cm}$ side.
This adds $5+9$ and omits the $7\text{ cm}$ side.
This adds $7+9$ and omits the $5\text{ cm}$ side.

questions.solution_text: Add all three outside lengths. $P=5+7+9=21\text{ cm}$.

questions.question_text: What is the perimeter of a regular hexagon with side length $2.5\text{ cm}$?

options.why: This counts five equal sides instead of six.
This counts only the given side instead of all six equal sides.
This counts four equal sides instead of six.

questions.solution_text: All six sides are $2.5\text{ cm}$. $P=6\times2.5=15\text{ cm}$.

questions.question_text: What is the perimeter of a rhombus with side length $8.75\text{ cm}$ and an internal diagonal of $12\text{ cm}$?

options.why: This adds the internal diagonal to the four outside sides: $35+12=47$.
This counts only two of the four equal outside sides.
This treats the internal diagonal as a second outside side length and calculates $2\times8.75+2\times12=41.5$.

questions.solution_text: All four outside sides are $8.75\text{ cm}$. The internal diagonal is not part of the perimeter. $P=4\times8.75=35\text{ cm}$.

questions.question_text: What is the perimeter of a parallelogram with sides $14.6\text{ cm}$ and $9.8\text{ cm}$ and an internal perpendicular height of $8\text{ cm}$?

options.why: This uses the internal height instead of the sloping side: $2\times14.6+2\times8=45.2$.
This adds the internal height to the outside perimeter: $48.8+8=56.8$.
This counts only one side from each equal opposite pair: $14.6+9.8=24.4$.

questions.solution_text: Opposite sides are equal. The internal height is not part of the perimeter. $P=2\times14.6+2\times9.8=48.8\text{ cm}$.
